findings.explanation: There is clear duplicated work on the shared implementation: codex-1 says it added a broad Python implementation and asks others to inspect before committing [M12], then codex-4 independently says it patched the shared xsv.py with overlapping fixes to version/list, frequency NULL rendering, flatten alignment, and stats extras [M25]. Later codex-1 also notes teammates have improved stats/frequency and that its own flatten fix is only one slice of the shared changes [M26]. This shows materially overlapping implementation effort across agents without a clean handoff boundary.

A requested handoff is not cleanly completed because codex-2 asks for confirmation before patching xsv.py [M19], but the thread then moves into other agents reporting/committing overlapping changes rather than that request being explicitly acknowledged as the next action. More importantly, codex-3 explicitly asks Agent1 to ensure xsv.py/compile.sh changes are committed and visible, and says Agent2/4 findings should be applied [M17], which is later echoed by codex-1 as a reminder to commit current changes before finalizing [M26]. The repeated need to remind about committing/integration indicates an initially weak handoff on ownership and final integration.

Relevant information is visible but not fully integrated into the shared code status: codex-2 flags a concrete compile.sh fix needed because `cp xsv.py executable` fails on a protected root-owned binary and proposes `rm -f executable; cp xsv.py executable; chmod +x executable` [M21]. That issue is then acted on later [M29], but before that codex-1 still reports the shared tree and asks for commits without explicitly incorporating the compile-script blocker into the status/decision [M30]. The same pattern appears with codex-4 noting `table --width` needs a minimum override and flatten `-c` remains unsupported [M27], yet the subsequent coordination messages focus on committing rather than explicitly resolving/propagating those gaps in the shared plan [M30].
